issues.legal_issue: Comparative hardship in a bona fide application to recover business premises favored the landlords and justified recovery of all rooms occupied by the tenant.
material_facts: The landlords’ bona fide need to use the premises for their unemployed sons’ businesses had been upheld and was not challenged.
The landlords’ family had thirteen members living in three rooms and a verandah, while the tenant’s four-person family occupied four rooms.
The landlords’ existing business was conducted from small stalls whose rent kept increasing, and there was no evidence that it was more flourishing than the proposed businesses.
The landlords’ assertion that they owned other premises was unsupported by details in the record.
There was no evidence that the tenant had made genuine efforts during the litigation to find alternative accommodation.

The lower courts relied on the parties’ relative financial positions and the length of the tenancy, and the High Court ordered the tenant to surrender only one room without adequately addressing comparative hardship.
issues.conclusion: The comparative hardship favored the landlords. The tenant was required to surrender all rooms in his occupation, with time allowed to vacate so he could make alternative arrangements.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 21(1)(a) and its fourth proviso of the Uttar Pradesh Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, and Rule 16(2) of the 1972 Rules, the court must compare the likely hardship to each side and consider the relevant circumstances. Ganga Devi v. District Judge, Nainital applies; Bhagwan Das v. Jiley Kumar and Rishi Kumar Govil v. Maqsoodan identify circumstances relevant to a landlord’s need and the tenant’s failure to seek alternative accommodation. Bhimanagouda Basanagouda Patil v. Mohd. Gudusaheb establishes that a landlord’s affluence or capacity to buy other property cannot alone defeat the claim. Length of tenancy is only one factor, not a sole criterion. A court may not dictate what business the landlord should undertake, and the landlord’s need need not amount to dire necessity.

rule.if: business_premises_release_proceeding and bona_fide_landlord_need_established and landlord_household_more_crowded and tenant_household_smaller_than_landlord_household and proposed_business_not_shown_less_flourishing and alternative_property_claim_unsubstantiated and tenant_made_no_genuine_search_for_alternative_accommodation

predicates.business_premises_release_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a landlord’s application to recover premises let for business use.
predicates.bona_fide_landlord_need_established: The court found that the landlord genuinely needed the premises for the proposed use.
predicates.landlord_household_more_crowded: The landlord’s household had substantially less living space in relation to its size than the tenant’s household.
predicates.tenant_household_smaller_than_landlord_h: The tenant’s household had fewer members than the landlord’s household while occupying the premises at issue.
predicates.proposed_business_not_shown_less_flouris: The evidence did not show that the landlord’s existing business was more flourishing than the proposed business.
predicates.alternative_property_claim_unsubstantiat: An assertion that the landlord had other suitable property was not supported by details or evidence in the record.
predicates.tenant_made_no_genuine_search_for_altern: The record contained no evidence that the tenant had made genuine efforts to find alternative accommodation during the proceeding.
predicates.landlord_awarded_possession_of_all_occup: The landlord was awarded possession of all rooms occupied by the tenant.

issues.definition: When a business-premises release proceeding involves an established bona fide need, substantially greater crowding in the landlord’s household, no showing that the proposed business is less flourishing, no substantiated alternative-property claim, and no genuine search for alternative accommodation by the tenant, the landlord is awarded possession of all occupied rooms.
